idiom_name: Foundation URLRequest (allHTTPHeaderFields + httpBody) / HTTPURLResponse; swift-nio HTTPRequestHead + body
implementation_notes: Foundation supplies the packaged forms: URLRequest carries allHTTPHeaderFields ([String: String]?) and value(forHTTPHeaderField:) for the header section plus httpBody: Data? (or httpBodyStream for large payloads) for the body, while URLResponse/HTTPURLResponse read metadata back from the reply; the system manages a few reserved headers itself (Content-Length, Host, Authorization, Connection, ...). On the server side swift-nio keeps the two sections separate as well - a request head with its HTTPHeaders and a body part streamed independently - which is the same split one layer down. A struct wrapper with a typed header enum is justified when the header vocabulary must be validated instead of living in a string dictionary.
code_sketch:
var req = URLRequest(url: url)
req.httpMethod = "POST"
req.setValue("order.created", forHTTPHeaderField: "X-Message-Type")
req.setValue(corr, forHTTPHeaderField: "X-Correlation-Id")
req.httpBody = try JSONEncoder().encode(order)     // body

let (data, response) = try await URLSession.shared.data(for: req)
let headers = (response as? HTTPURLResponse)?.allHeaderFields
pitfalls: Reserved headers (Content-Length, Host, Authorization, Connection, ...) are managed by the URL loading system: setting them is ignored or rewritten, so code that tries to control framing manually is silently corrected.
URLRequest is a value type - mutating a copy inside a helper that takes it by value drops the change unless the function writes back inout or returns the request.
URLSession.data(for:) buffers the whole body in memory; large payloads belong in upload/download tasks or httpBodyStream, not in httpBody.
